claim: For failures that leave the scene in a state the task policy cannot continue from (a toppled or jammed object), learning separate object-reset skills, collected from failure states that a multimodal language model finds in rollout videos, adds success beyond what retry-style augmentation alone gives. Supported only if removing the reset skills lowers success on every coffee and assembly setting tested, if replacing the language model's decisions with a human's raises success further, and if the language model sorts failure videos into retryable versus needing a reset with at least 85% accuracy against human labels.

experiments: Build the training data and system. Setup: for each of nine RoboMimic tasks (Coffee, Stack, StackThree, Threading, ThreePieceAssembly at randomisation levels D0 and D1), expand 10 human demonstrations to 500 with MimicGen and insert, at the start and between subtasks, a random arm displacement (up to 45 degrees and 0.5 m) followed by an interpolated motion back to the next subtask's start; train only on the return motion plus the following task actions, never on the random displacement. Run the resulting policy for hundreds of episodes, have Gemini-2.5-Pro label each failure video (retryable or reset-required, object to reset, interacting objects, time of failure), restore the logged simulator state at that time, collect 20 human reset demonstrations per object, place the interacting objects together in new scenes and expand to 500 with the same augmentation. Fine-tune pi0.5 with one LoRA adapter for the task and one per reset skill; at run time an online language-model monitor swaps in a reset adapter when it judges the scene unrecoverable and swaps back afterwards. 50 trials per task.

Ablate the reset skills. Setup: on Coffee and ThreePieceAssembly at D0 and D1, compare the full system, the system without reset skills (augmentation only), reset skills without the augmentation, and the full system with a human choosing when and which reset to run. Result: 96 / 78 / 62 / 58% for the full system, 92 / 74 / 60 / 54% without reset skills, 88 / 64 / 60 / 50% with reset skills only, and 100 / 90 / 68 / 64% with human decisions.

Measure how well each reset skill works on its own. Setup: separate environments with randomised scenes where success means restoring the reset object: coffee machine lid and coffee pod; T-shaped and U-shaped blocks; also the share of reset demonstrations that generate successfully. Result: lid 84% and T-block 88%, but coffee pod 24% and U-block 20%, which need re-grasping and re-orienting a toppled object; generation efficiency 83.7% and 48.6% versus 11.6% and 5.9%.

Check the language model's failure analysis against people. Setup: hand-label 50 execution videos each for Coffee and ThreePieceAssembly and score Gemini-2.5-Pro on retry-versus-reset classification, which object to reset, and the failure timestamp. Result: 88% and 96% on retry versus reset, 88% and 78% on the reset object, and 78% and 66% on the timestamp.
